statement: A moving walkway at an airport is $60$ meters long. Standing still on it, Zara is carried from one end to the other in $60$ seconds. Walking at her usual pace on the walkway, in the direction it moves, she gets from one end to the other in $20$ seconds. How many seconds would it take her to walk $60$ meters at the same usual pace on the floor beside the walkway?

choices.misconception: I treated the walkway like a second walker and added the rates, 1/20 + 1/60 = 1/15 of the length per second, so I got 15 seconds.
I thought her speed while walking on the walkway was just her walking speed, so I kept the 20 seconds.
I subtracted the two times, 60 - 20 = 40, instead of subtracting the two speeds.
I added the two times, 20 + 60 = 80, as if she had to do both trips.

hints: Find the speed of the walkway, and Zara's speed while walking on it.
The walkway moves $1$ meter per second, and walking on it she moves $3$ meters per second.
Her own walking speed is the difference, $3 - 1 = 2$ meters per second.

solutions.reliable: The walkway moves $60 / 60 = 1$ meter per second. Walking on it, Zara moves $60 / 20 = 3$ meters per second, which is her walking speed plus the walkway's speed. So she walks at $3 - 1 = 2$ meters per second, and $60$ meters on the floor takes her $60 / 2 = 30$ seconds.
solutions.elegant: In $60$ seconds of walking on the walkway she would cover $3$ walkway lengths, and the walkway itself supplies $1$ of those. So her legs cover $2$ lengths in $60$ seconds, which is $1$ length in $30$ seconds.

author: Devansh Sanghavi
